   -i <path to directory>,  --replaydirectory <path to directory>

item.text: Production is now pinned down: the owned tile gains its production value after a blank move, starting on the second turn-state line. I’m checking turn-limit scaling next so the engine loop matches the original instead of just the per-turn mechanics.

The small-board move probe exposed an important edge case: after a losing move, the owner map can still report the moving player on a zero-strength origin square for at least one frame. I’m adding a scripted-response bot so I can step through those transitions turn by turn instead of repeating one move forever.

Direction mapping is now fixed: `0` stay, `1` north, `2` east, `3` south, `4` west. The remaining mechanics risk is player-vs-player combat, so I’m searching for the smallest deterministic two-player map that exposes collisions cleanly.

I found another non-obvious behavior: on multiplayer runs the engine can rewrite the requested dimensions to a different actual board size. I’m using one of those reduced two-player boards now because it gives a clean collision test for simultaneous player-vs-player movement.

The first game-mechanics comparison found the right fault line: I was letting neutral cells deal adjacent damage, which the reference clearly does not. I’m narrowing neutral damage to same-square only and rerunning the exact same probe before touching anything else.

The next mismatch is narrower: player units are damaging adjacent neutrals in my engine, and the reference does not. I’m changing damage resolution so only same-square combat involves neutrals; adjacent combat is player-vs-player only.
